About

About SmartHome-AI

An independent project about local, open-source smart homes and automation that works in the real world.

3 min read

In this guide

  • Editorial principles
  • Topics covered
  • About the language
  • How this site is built
  • Who writes it
  • Contact and corrections

SmartHome-AI started from a common frustration: most smart home content is either product marketing, or so technical that it assumes you already know what an MQTT broker is.

The commitment here is different: explain the why before the how, with examples that work in real homes — including homes with unstable internet, thick walls and people who would rather not think about technology.

Editorial principles#

  1. Local first. The cloud is a convenience, never a dependency.
  2. Open source whenever possible. Home Assistant, ESPHome, Zigbee2MQTT, Frigate, Scrypted.
  3. No sponsored lists. When a product is named, it is because it solves a described problem.
  4. Plan B matters. Every automation must work — or fail safely — when something goes down.
  5. Respect for the people living there. Automation that annoys the household is bad automation.

Topics covered#

  • Home Assistant — the platform
  • ESPHome and ESP32 — devices you build yourself
  • Zigbee2MQTT and ZHA and the ZBT-1 / ZBT-2 dongles
  • Matter and Thread — the standard that crosses ecosystems
  • MQTT — the postal service of the smart home
  • Apple HomeKit — iPhone, Siri and Apple TV
  • Scrypted, Frigate and cameras and AI cameras
  • Claude and MCP and OpenClaw — AI at home
  • Hardware, networking and CasaOS / umbrelOS

About the language#

The guide library is written in Brazilian Portuguese and is being translated into English progressively. Configuration files, YAML and command examples are language-neutral, and browser translation handles these pages well in the meantime.

How this site is built#

This is a static site: HTML, CSS and JavaScript with no frameworks, generated by a Python script from Markdown files, versioned on GitHub and published on Cloudflare. No database, no trackers, no ads — it loads fast even on a bad mobile connection.
